A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, including their figures, tables and appendices, and describe the same 17-attack, 160-question study. Despite v3's new JailbreakRadar title and substantial reorganization, corresponding material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original jailbreak and defense experiments, transfer attacks, runtime and token measurements, longitudinal tests, and human validation of response judging.

after.justification: V3 retains those original empirical results and adds DeepSeek-V3 measurements, an AdvBench category audit, and human annotation of policy categories.

M1.justification: The attack procedures, six-category taxonomy and three-label judging rule are retained. Renaming Parameter-Based to Generation-Parameter-Based and moving attack descriptions to Appendix G do not introduce new algorithmic components.

E1.justification: The same 160-question, 16-category jailbreak task and AdvBench-derived training coverage remain. DeepSeek-V3 adds a target model within the existing black-box scenario; the AdvBench audit samples an existing source. The renamed child-related category remains excluded from attack evaluation.

E2.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 17 attacks, direct-query baseline, eight defenses and combined-defense configuration. The judging-method comparison also retains string matching and a single-label judge; additional citations do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: V3 adds DeepSeek-V3 as an API-accessed target and introduces protocols for auditing 100 AdvBench questions and classifying policies by three-annotator unanimity. The stated default temperature changes from 0.1 in v2 Table 10 to 0.01 in v3 Appendix F. The PDFs do not establish whether experiments were rerun; attack budgets and metrics remain.

E4.justification: V3 Appendix C.2 adds a quantitative audit of AdvBench's category coverage and imbalance, while Appendix B.3 adds general/specific policy annotations. Existing transferability, token-length, runtime and longitudinal analyses are retained and reorganized into Appendix A, with limited extensions for DeepSeek-V3.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix A.2 explicitly reports three repetitions and mean/standard-deviation reporting; Tables 2, 3, 5 and 6 display standard deviations. V3 removes both that repetition statement and those deviations without replacement uncertainty reporting, substantially reducing statistical transparency. The judge-validation agreement statistics remain.

E6.justification: Shared-target direct and transfer means remain unchanged. New DeepSeek-V3 results include LAA's 1.00 direct ASR; its overall mean changes from 0.85 across eight targets to 0.87 across nine. Defense aggregates and dataset-audit counts also change. However, the new transfer heatmap in Figure 4(c) has method-label inconsistencies relative to Table 5, limiting interpretation of those detailed results.

T1.justification: The ASR and bypass-rate definitions are preserved, and neither version contains original theorems or proofs. Added taxonomy explanations and policy groupings are conceptual and empirical rather than new mathematical results.

C1.justification: V3 explicitly claims the most comprehensive dataset/provider coverage and specifies novelty in covering automatic and non-automatic attacks. Its abstract replaces blanket statements about powerful attacks with a qualified claim about heuristic attacks' low practicality under defenses. The underlying taxonomy, dataset and unified-evaluation contributions remain.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands interpretation through general/specific policy distinctions, safety–utility explanations for high baseline ASRs, and hypotheses about severe-category phrase detection. Its limitations newly address static policies, within-category question differences, training-data overlap and annotator biases. These materially broaden the qualifications surrounding the benchmark's meaning and applicability.

D1.justification: V3 specifies gpt-4-turbo for response judging, documents default or absent system prompts, identifies DeepSeek's official API, and describes annotator qualifications and attack-selection criteria. These are additional disclosures; hardware specifications and most per-attack configurations are retained and relocated.

R1.justification: V3 adds explicit comparisons with h4rm3l, Xu et al.'s comprehensive study and Yi et al.'s survey in Appendix I.3. Additional references support its judging approach, taxonomy rationale and DeepSeek evaluation. This sharpens positioning against earlier evaluations and concurrent work while retaining the existing background.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, settings and findings are extensively revised. Detailed attack descriptions, ablations and related work move into dedicated appendices A–K, while the main taxonomy becomes more compact. Separate limitations, ethical considerations and acknowledgements sections substantially reshape the document.

P2.justification: The combined defense table is split into ASR and bypass-rate tables. Heatmaps are regrouped, with Llama3.1 promoted to the main text and earlier panels retained in appendices. DeepSeek panels and columns, dataset-count and hardware tables are added; runtime displays are consolidated and numerous figures and tables are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: V3 adds useful DeepSeek measurements and an AdvBench audit, and clarifies policy interpretation and limitations. However, it removes v2's explicit three-run reporting and table standard deviations. Its new DeepSeek transfer heatmap also labels a column averaging 0.45 as LAA, whereas Table 5 reports 0.85 for LAA. The informational gains coexist with reduced statistical transparency and inconsistent presentation of new evidence, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
